definitions.gloss: blanching; briefly passing through hot water
definitions.explanation: a cooking technique where ingredients are briefly dipped in boiling water to soften, remove impurities, or set color

examples.japanese: ⟦{刺身|さしみ}→刺身：04023_sashimi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{湯通|ゆどお}し⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
⟦{肉|にく}→肉：02240_niku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{湯通|ゆどお}し⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧{臭|くさ}み⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}る→取る：00565_toru⟧。
examples.english: Blanch the meat to remove the smell.

examples.japanese: ⟦{豆腐|とうふ}→豆腐：04928_toufu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{湯通|ゆどお}し⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧おく⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{崩|くず}れ→崩れる：04248_kuzureru⟧にくい。
examples.english: If you blanch tofu beforehand, it's less likely to fall apart.

notes:
COOKING TECHNIQUE:
{湯通|ゆどお}し involves briefly dipping ingredients in boiling water. The name comes from ⟦{湯|ゆ}→湯：01740_yu⟧ (hot water) + ⟦{通|とお}す→通す：02300_toosu⟧ (to pass through).

PURPOSES:
- Remove fishy or meaty odors
- Remove excess oil or fat
- Soften texture slightly
- Set color in vegetables
- Firm up delicate ingredients like tofu

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{刺身|さしみ}→刺身：04023_sashimi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{湯通|ゆどお}し - blanching sashimi (creates "tataki" texture)
- ⟦{肉|にく}→肉：02240_niku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{湯通|ゆどお}し - removing impurities from meat before cooking
- ⟦{野菜|やさい}→野菜：02265_yasai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{湯通|ゆどお}し - brightening vegetable colors

SIMILAR TECHNIQUES:
- ⟦{茹|ゆ}でる→茹でる：02324_yuderu⟧ - to boil (longer cooking time)
- {下茹|したゆ}で - parboiling (slightly longer than {湯通|ゆどお}し)
- ⟦{霜降|しもふ}り→霜降り：18934_shimofuri⟧ - same technique for meat/fish
